text: Old Garrick leans over his stall, eyes twinkling.
Old Garrick: A birthday, is it? Well, your coin buys any one of these.
A paper twist of honey sweets.
A ribbon the colour of cornflowers.
A little wooden bird, carved by hand.
Old Garrick: Sweets for the sweet.
He wraps them tight in brown paper.
Old Garrick: She'll wear that till it's rags.
He folds it neatly into your palm.
Old Garrick: Took me a week, that one. It'll last her a lifetime.
